chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Getting Chuckles interested again
summary: Following Bubbles' idea, Green pretends to learn steps and asks J. D. if he is doing them right, coaxing him back; nobody learns all of Bubbles' steps.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: But Chuckles, you said, was losing interest in tap dancing?

Well, that's the way I explained it because, see -- I mean he didn't seem to -- he wasn't as happy about tap dancing as I thought anyone that could do tap dancing should be, you know. I thought they were all happy people like, you know, and he was -- I guess he was maturing, you know. Maybe he missed his mother or something, you know.

And -- but it worked out like Mr. Bubbles said, you know. If I like learn a step or pretended that I was in the process of learning one of Mr. Bubbles' steps, and I could ask him, 'Hey, Chuckles, how am I doing?' I didn't call him Chuckles at that time. I called him J. D. 'Am I doing this right?' See, that was Mr. Bubbles' idea to kind of bring him
around. So that's what I did.

Yes, it did. See -- but, well, J. D., he tried the steps a few times, you know, and then -- I say, "Am I doing it right? Do you think this is right?" He said, "Well, let me see. I think he done it thisaway", and, you know, that was Mr. Bubbles' idea to get him to talking that way, and he would try the step out.

And then you tell him if he's doing it right or wrong, and then you say, "I think we better ask Mr. Bubbles, get him to show the both of us. He'll tell us if we're doing it correctly." And then he say, "Well, when I get him -- get you there, start explaining the correct way to do the steps, I take him on. I teach him how to do me", which he's supposed to really be doing, you see.

So that's what happened, but I mean J. D. still didn't learn all of Mr. Bubbles steps, which nobody in the world could Learn. Nobody, I didn't think, because I knew more of his steps than anyone, and I couldn't even do all of Mr. Bubbles' steps, you see.
